scale.sizeBasis: Brightness converted to a reference-sphere size; not resolved dimensions or measured volume.
scale.uncertaintyInterpretation: Author sensitivity estimate approximately -15/+30 percent for assumed albedo ±0.02 and H ±0.1 mag; not a measured Gaussian 1-sigma interval. Published rounded diameter/radius need not be exact doubles.
scale.referenceRadiusUse: Adopt the body-page nominal radius, as Kiviuq does, and use it as equal-volume display scale only. Do not recompute it from rounded H or silently substitute the older 122-body table diameter.

displayOrientation.phaseEpoch: display reference only; no measured W0 or landmark epoch
displayOrientation.spinSense: Reported retrograde sense; no time propagation
displayOrientation.displayPeriodUse: The reported rotation period is an informational fact. The prepared scene uses a fixed arbitrary display phase and does not propagate physical spin
displayOrientation.qualification: Partial observed south-ecliptic pole latitude and retrograde sense are preserved. Exact pole longitude and current phase remain unknown; ecliptic south is a representative display convention, not the full measured pole. Author body-page pole cells are blank; the primary paper supplies this partial constraint.

selectedEclipticPole.meaning: Ecliptic south is a chosen representative within the measured latitude interval; longitude undefined at the pole, not a measured zero.

conversion.formula: Ecliptic (0,0,-1) rotated by J2000 obliquity -> ICRF (0,sin(epsilon),-cos(epsilon)); RA=90 deg, Dec=epsilon-90 deg.

shapeLimit: Published south-ecliptic pole latitude approximately -85 ± 15 degrees and sidereal period are useful; do not invent a pole longitude or native convex mesh.
sourceDiscrepancies: Individual page lists pole unknown; primary 2018 §3.2(l) gives beta=-85 ±15 deg and retrograde spin. Use the partial primary constraint; do not invent pole longitude.
